Gilded Shell

The Gilded Shell is a gigantic tortoise-shaped building situated in the Dawn Gate district of Katapesh. The surface of the building is covered with gleaming metal plates, designed and installed by a master armorer named Malthus Feyhew.

Feyhew and his staff of apprentices and journeymen craft high-quality and greatly valued suits of armor, all of masterwork quality. The master armorer tasks special interest in unusual materials, and keeps a standing offer to his clients to build custom armor from such materials at a 50-percent discount. He also keeps an inventory of special and unusual armors, including giant scorpion shells, blink dog hides, gorgon hides, gray render hides, Naga scales, bone mail, and wyvern hides.⁠
1735974853:
Supplicant Properties

The Supplicant Properties aren't the most luxurious houses in the city, but Kalistocrats who live in the manor houses of other districts pay thousands of gold pieces to spend at least one night here. Once a year, the High Prophet chooses one of these properties, and its residents have the honor of entering the High Prophet's Sanctum and discussing any topic they wish with him without limitations.⁠

Arvensoar

Arvensoar is the tower built by local Varisians and the citizens of Magnimar to replace the Seacleft Spire after it was destroyed by an angelic being. It took over 18 years to create the tower, but it now stands as a symbol of the city's receptiveness to the guidance of good spirits.⁠

At approximately 400 feet in height, the tower is the tallest structure in Magnimar and stands over the districts of Lowcleft and Naos. The tower serves as the barracks and fortress for the local city watch and is defended with eight powerful trebuchets able to target any attackers regardless of the direction from which they attack.⁠⁠
1763594173:
Veldraine

The town of Veldraine is perhaps the most important strategic holding of Korvosa, and the second-oldest Chelaxian settlement in Varisia.

Located at the mouth of Conqueror's Bay, Veldraine's ships make up most of the Korvosan Navy, and its naval academy trains most of the city-state's sailors and captains. It also contains a giant winch that allows the military to pull an immense chain taut across the entrance to the bay, keeping invading navies or pirates out of the waters—or trapped within it to be dispatched one by one.⁠⁠ The chain is inspected monthly by Korvosan officials, and has only been used once in 4685 AR in order to fight pirates from Riddleport.⁠
1767451963:
Rolan's Shop

Rolan's Shop is a tinker's shop that sells automatons and other engineering products, although in 4710 AR, its owner, Rolan, went a little crazy with all the chaos in the city and barricaded the roads around his shop and attacked anyone who approached.⁠
1776599783:
Palin's Lighthouse

Palin's Lighthouse can be found on the small Jeggare Isle in Conqueror's Bay, and is part of the Varisian city of Korvosa. It is the only structure on the island,⁠ and is presumably named after Captain Keyra Palin, a hero from the early years of Korvosa's history.⁠
1785967753:
Cliffside Millworks

Cliffside Millworks is a factory that has abandoned grain production and focused on ambitious machine part manufacturing projects. Complex clockwork designs allow the factory to create most of its parts without human intervention, and its quality rivals that of Korvosa. The owner is Jerich Ableton, although Obo, the former slave, is the true mastermind behind the factory's designs.⁠

Lost Fortress of Mekshir

The Lost Fortress of Mekshir guarded the trade routes from Osirion to its province of Thuvia until it was buried in a sandstorm during the khamsin season of -841 AR. The fortress is rumored to contain treasures including an armory of magical weapons and several months of payroll, but is said to be guarded by the undead.⁠
1801330963:
Wolfpoint

Wolfpoint is the name of an Isgeri fort located north of the Chitterwood on the Conerica River, about 25 miles southwest of the town of Saringallow. It houses approximately 300 soldiers and their officers, many of whom are veterans of the recent Goblinblood Wars. The fort itself consists of several wooden barracks surrounded by a tall log palisade. Much of the palisade was destroyed during the wars and has since been rebuilt, although many sections still show signs of fire damage and goblin blood.⁠⁠
1804916343:
Shadow Clock

The Shadow Clock is a 250-foot-tall clocktower in Magnimar's Underbridge district. It is a rusting and leaning structure of stone, wood, and metal. Like the rest of Underbridge it is in constant shadow from the Irespan. An angelic statue is positioned atop the tower, and the clock is frozen at 3 o'clock.⁠

At least 10 people have died trying to climb the inside stairs, which earned them the nickname "Terrible Stairs". While ordered closed by the city, this tower still stands.⁠

Local rumors say ghosts or other nasty inhabitants reside in the tower. However, as of 4712 AR it was the lair of the Scarecrow, a flesh golem made over 100 years ago by the Brothers of the Seven.⁠⁠
1812213713:
Fancy Reefclaw

The Fancy Reefclaw is a gaudily painted, but successful, brewery located in Magnimar's Lowcleft district. The front is painted red and yellow, with an image of a well-dressed reefclaw. Owned by House Deverin, it is operated day-to-day by Golliver Haskinswurth. The brewery is best known for its raspberry ale and lambics.⁠⁠
1814235183:
Olivine Tomb of Djederet II

Little is known about the Olivine Tomb of Djederet II, located in Osirion during its First Age in what is now Thuvia.⁠⁠ Its namesake pharaoh Djederet II was the nephew of Hakotep I and succeeded him as Osirion's ruler in -1611 AR, and is known for reverting many of the Sky Pharaoh's works.⁠
1814331873:
Bloodsalt

Bloodsalt is the largest of several ruined cities on the shore of Terwa Lake, at the northern edge of Rechiend's Plains in the Mwangi Expanse. It takes its name from the region's red, iron-rich silt (similar to that which gave Bloodcove its name). Much of the city is now buried beneath the silt. The local tribes view the ruins as taboo. Treasure hunters who survive the creatures living within the ruins also have to escape the wrath of the natives. Few clues remain to identify the city's original inhabitants, but visitors tell of uncovering skeletons whose various locations imply the entire population died at once. In fact, the lake occasionally releases a cloud of deadly volcanic gas, which kills everything in the vicinity. The city is also sometimes known as the City of the Dragon-Men, after iconography found there which depicts people sprouting dragon-like wings and flying off to commune with spirits.⁠
1817196623:
Withrun House

Spiro Spero

The ancient ruined fortress of Spiro Spero lies north of the Ndele Gap, on the Mwangi Expanse side of the Shattered Range. It takes its name from the spiral pathway that winds its way up the mountainside to its gate.⁠
1861601983:
Qadlus Mavari

Qadlus Mavari is a Qadiran city located in the Northern Zho Mountains area, and is the north-easternmost settlement in Qadira.⁠ Qadlus Mavari is a flourishing oasis town built around a shrine dedicated to Lugalisimaru, the so called "Palm Tree King". The town does a healthy trade in selling offerings that can be left at other shrines to Lugalisimaru that are built at each of the oases that dot the desert beyond. Qadlus Mavari also boasts a booming trade in water-producing magic items.⁠
1862098733:
Ryvanthnyl

Ryvanthnyl is a memorial located in the eastern part of Kyonin. The site is dedicated to the lives and traditions of people and cultures that perished and are remembered by the elves who preserve their memory by leaving behind works of art and objects of significance.⁠

Ryvanthnyl is protected by gravekeepers and preserved through magic that safeguards the objects within, though the origin, era, and historical significance of many of these objects remain unknown.⁠
1863591883:
Jaha

Jaha is a great crumbling city in the northern part of the Mwangi Jungle in the Mwangi Expanse.⁠⁠⁠⁠
1864856393:
Volod

Volod is a small Iobarian town in the Norinor built in 4400 AR to replace the former logging town of Hroran. Located on the Noyrus River, the town has been dominated by logging and woodcrafting trades for much of its history. As of 4710 AR, strange events had recently been occurring around Volod, and the town's druids spoke of new deities in the highlands and Norinor who demanded worship.⁠
1864944523:
Thrashing Badger

The Thrashing Badger was a rough-and-ready bar in the Yolubilis Harbor district of Kintargo that burned to the ground during the Night of Ashes. Before its destruction, The Thrashing Badger was home not just to rowdy sailors and labourers but also served as a drinking hole for a myriad of malcontents and rebels, most of whom now drink at nearby Clenchjaw's instead.⁠

As of 4724 AR, many attempts to rebuild the tavern have variously failed.⁠

Commonfield

Commonfield is more of a collection of pesh-farming homesteads in western Katapesh than a town, but it represents the nation's densest concentration of pesh farming. Twenty-two farmers, their families, and their hired hands call Commonfield's 36 farms home. These farmers are, for the most part, hardworking and honest; their crops are precious, requiring them to post guards at night.

The five wealthiest farmers meet weekly to discuss coordinating guard patrols, how the season fares, any insect or rodent pests affecting the crop, and other topics. Two notable members of the council are the aiuvarin Richele Gerst and the halfling Kerek Cullstone.⁠
1893564373:
Kora

The settlement of Kora, the seat of the Rampore Isles' administration in the Shackles, is surrounded by rice and sugar plantations. The crops are sold to the less self-sufficient islands in the Shackles, and the trained slaves who work these fields also serve as a commodity to be traded to slavers. Brutal overseers run the operations and mercilessly exploit the slave labor.⁠
1896946113:
Tregan

Tregan is a small town⁠ on the border of Taldor and Galt, and is renowned as a refuge for Galtan refugees of the Red Revolution, who make up a fair percentage of the population.⁠ The Reconciliation Council is working to reunite expatriates with their loved ones now that the revolution as finally ended and the town is experiencing a boost in population that is finding hard to accommodate.⁠

Among the town's businesses is the Hornet's Nest tavern, owned by the bard Vallyn.⁠
1904225593:
Fort Hazard

Fort Hazard stands on the bluffs overlooking Port Peril, capital of the Shackles. Its strategic position allows it to control both the town and the harbour. It was the stronghold of the late former Hurricane King Kerdak Bonefist.⁠⁠ The tallest of its seven defensive towers is also the location of the lighthouse known as Besmara's Beacon.⁠
1917631173:
Fort Bandu

Fort Bandu is a fortification in eastern Vidrian, located in the Bandu Hills on the banks of the River of Lost Tears near the border with the Mwangi Expanse.⁠
1920450453:
Temple of the Sunken Sign

The Temple of the Sunken Sign is a Ghol-Gani temple complex dedicated to Azathoth, hidden in the Sodden Lands.
1930674163:
Aerduin's Folly

Aerduin was the capital of the Arch-Duchy of Melcat until the coming of the Living God, Razmir. When Duke Melcat refused to pledge his fealty to Razmir, the wizard destroyed the town and all of his inhabitants. Now known as Aerduin's Folly, the ruins have lain abandoned for 50 years.⁠
1951057633:
Dobrova

Dobrova is a small Irriseni town on the Marbleflow River in the province of Wintercrux. As of 4713 AR it struggled under the notorious distinction of having the nation's highest taxes, thanks to its new ruler, Baron Vasyl Yelizaveta.⁠
1951859663:
Wreck of the Kaijitsu Star

The Wreck of the Kaijitsu Star is in better condition than its sister ship, Kaijitsu's Blossom, because its smaller size allowed it to sink deeper into the swamp and was protected from the violent waves. For a time, a cannibal goblin named Vorka used it as a base until Licktoad goblins set the ship ablaze with fireworks.⁠
1963214063:
Chainhouse

The Chainhouse is the base of operations for Pangolais's Chainguard. The three-story building boasts formidable defenses, and its central location provides easy access to any neighborhood within the city. The Chainguard's "captain" is Irciele, a pragmatic woman with no time for dealing with the theatrics of the Midnight Lord's loyal followers. The building's prison primarily serves as a short-term detention center; those who break the law are sent to the nearby Cathedral of Exquisite Agony, where they are tortured in most cases.⁠

Ravenous Sphinx

The Ravenous Sphinx is a huge statue in the shape of a crouching jet-black lion topped by the snarling head of a fantastic beast. It is located in the Parched Dunes of Osirion, in the shadow of the Brazen Peaks, partially buried in the desert's sands.⁠ It houses three large rooms, with a connecting central antechamber.⁠
1987743033:
Robu

Robu is a small town on the second largest island of the Ushinawa Isles in the Shackles.

The residents of Robu have done their best to eradicate the obscene reminders of its earlier Ghol-Gan occupants. A native evil, the penanggalan named Tiktakara, has laired in the woodlands outside of Robu and entertains herself by tormenting the town's residents and converting its women into subservient manananggals. The Lord of Robu, Kensai Hikarogawa, offers a bounty to any adventurers who can rid the town of this menace.⁠
1991340243:
Great Tower

As a dominant point on Korvosa's skyline, the Great Tower rivals some of the ancient buildings of the city for height. This modern tower is used by the Sable Company as a military base and training centre for hippogriff riders.⁠
1997160263:
Merciful Bay

Merciful Bay is a large port town on Taldor's Inner Sea coast, located between the towns of Kozan to the north, and Golsifar to the south.⁠
2001272473:
Sphinx Gate

The Sphinx Gate is located in the northwest of Absalom and is usually open even at night due to the constant traffic in the area. It connects to the farms of the region and is used by the First Guard to patrol the Cairnlands, taking its name from the enormous sphinx statue erected there. During the Unraveling Siege, when the proteans attacked the city, dozens of riddles appeared at the gate, and after a guard solved one, the proteans were no longer able to dominate the city's skies, proving instrumental in the victory against them.⁠ Only those who have aided Absalom on countless occasions have access to the riddles, as no one knows what dangerous magic they may contain, and of all the city's entrances, this is the only one that has never been breached, partly due to its proximity to the Azlanti Keep.⁠
2008684063:
Jarvis Estate

Jarvis Estate, located in The Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of House Jarvis.⁠⁠
2008736563:
Crying Leaf

Crying Leaf is an isolated elven village in Varisia's Mierani Forest. It is a day's travel from the ruins of the former elf city of Celwynvian, where the elves are engaged in a bitter struggle with the drow. As a result, it is used by the elves as a staging ground for their warriors, including contingents of Lantern Bearers, and is not entirely safe from drow raids.

The village consists mainly of simple, low stone and wooden structures, decorated with graceful carvings. It is protected by a wall of thorns. Most of the village's trade and supplies arrive from Kyonin through the use of magic—there is little contact with Riddleport and the rest of neighbouring Varisia. Non-elven visitors are rare.

The leader of the village is the sorcerer Eviana Nirgassan, who was appointed by Kyonin a decade ago following the assassination of her predecessor by the drow.⁠

Sumitha

Sumitha is an ancient Ghol-Gani ruin on the Island of Empty Eyes in the Shackles.⁠

Dustpawn

Dustpawn is a small town in eastern Isger, about seven miles from the Conerica River and close to the border with Druma, and was founded in 4324 AR.⁠
2049603523:
Ranage's Circle

Ranage's Circle is a tight-knit circle of massive cypress trees in the heart of the Mwangi Jungle. It was planted 1,000 years ago by druids of the Jambala Jaeg tribe. The ancient magic of the circle protects against evil creatures and hostile wildlife, making it a safe resting place for those who know how to find it. The tree at the centre of the circle has a split trunk, which is wrapped tightly around a black stone. According to legend, the stone is the prison of Golokango, who is either a demon or a powerful jungle spirit. The central tree is barely alive, and according to the legend is a arboreal regent druid who sacrificed most of its life force to seal the prison. Some tales even claim that the guardian is a sibling of Dimari-Diji, the incredibly ancient arboreal regent of Osibu.⁠

Among its guardians is Temteki, an earth elemental that resembles a tree.⁠
2052591193:
Harvest's End

Harvest's End is a small village located near where the Rimeflow River and the Iceflow River meet in the Bleakmarch region of Irrisen. The village mainly sustains itself from fishing and trade, with the traveling merchants standing out sharply with their colorful clothes next to drab woolen clothes of the villagers. The town also has a ferry for merchants and lumberers to cross the Rimeflow River operated by an ice troll named Rimetusk.⁠

Rimetusk serves as the de facto leader of the town after allowing his ego to grow too large, since the town's isolation from Whitethrone means that Rimetusk communicates infrequently with the Jadwiga to whom he is supposed to report.

Falchion Point

Falchion Point is a small town in the Widowmaker Isle in the Shackles. Falchion Point has a reputation for unshowy fighting. The town is known for the Bloody Twins event, in which two combatants are manacled together and fight one another with glass shards. Usually, both opponents in a battle of Bloody Twins end up bleeding to death. Lefty Kemya, Falchion Point's mayor, is famous for having actually survived the Bloody Twins, albeit at the cost of his right hand.

Other attractions include Beaten Eyes, wherein four combatants are temporarily blinded with magic and pitted against one another in a bare-knuckle battle. Another unnamed game of wits is also played that involves two heavily armored combatants who duel in a small pit the ground of which is covered in hidden deadly traps.⁠

Sharpened Axe

The Sharpened Axe of Urgir in the Hold of Belkzen is a fighting school located on the southeastern side of the city's fourth level.⁠

Siavenian

Siavenian is a small town in the northern Fierani Forest of Kyonin, just east of the Endowhar River. It grew up around a disused elf gate that was activated by a group of adventurers fleeing the Darklands in 4708 AR.⁠

After the Godsrain the elf gate melted into a pile of strange metallic liquid that none have dare touch yet.⁠
2072729153:
Mount Kla

Mount Kla is the 12th-tallest peak of the Five Kings Range at 14,411 feet.⁠ It is located in the central parts of the range east of Emperor's Peak and west of the Verduran Forest⁠ and is visible from the sunlit East End of Highhelm's King's Crown layer.⁠⁠
2096845863:
Solscrene

Solscrene is located on the stretch of the Sellen River within the Verduran Forest, and it faces Andoran on the river's opposite bank. As one travels north from Cassomir to the Isle of Arenway, Solscrene is considered to be the last village before one reaches the true deep forest. Solscrene sits on a small craggy island and its inhabitants are rather insular, constantly circulating foul stories about distant Galtans, neighbouring Andorens, the mysterious druids of Arenway and even gnomes.⁠
2120330563:
Sarini Estate

Sarini Estate, located in the Greens district of Kintargo, Ravounel, is the home of House Sarini.⁠⁠ Most of its Thrune-loyalist residents fled Kintargo after the Kintargan Rebellion.⁠
2121720233:
Hagby

The small trading town of Hagby is located on Glacier Lake in the Irriseni capital province of Thronehold.⁠

Hagby is the last stop for all trade headed to Whitethrone from the west. It is ruled with paranoid scrutiny by the cruel Baroness Ladina. The peasants do not trust anyone knowing that even a hint of the slightest misdemeanor results in harsh punishments. A lot of peasants work their daily duties with missing fingers, eye patches and worse. Yefrem Chelnitsky is the despicable agent of the baroness. He follows her everywhere, with parchment and quill in hand to record every demand and directive his mistress utters.⁠

Despite the overbearing atmosphere, the Heralds of Summer's Return have a lot of members in Hagby including warehouse worker Nakia Serebrynakova and blacksmith Yuri Patasil.⁠
2125578413:
Marching Springs

The Marching Springs are a 30 square mile region of Nirmathas between the Fangwood and the Mindspin Mountains. Geysers erupt in a procession through the region.⁠
2127437973:
Gold Canyon

Gold Canyon is not a natural canyon but rather the remains of an ancient strip mine used in Taldor's early history. It is located in Meratt County within Tandak Prefecture, east of Cassomir.⁠ The ravine is 80 feet wide, 30 feet deep, and runs for almost 10 miles in total, and its bottom is filled with stagnant water.⁠

It once had a stone bridge crossing it, but this collapsed decades ago during a small earthquake. While it is the responsibility of Baron Telus, he has shown no interest in repairing the structure.⁠ Locals on foot can still cross the canyon relatively easily due to steps cut into the canyon's already stepped sides, but this route is impassable for horses and wagons.⁠

Gold Canyon once boosted a rich vein of gold and quartz that was mined out over 4,000 years ago, and most of the metal was used to mint early Taldan currency. The canyon is thus a minor holy site of Abadar, and local worshippers make small pilgrimages to the site. Such followers search the bottom of the canyon for any remaining gold, taking even a small flake of it as a sign of Abadar's favour. Unbeknownst to these pilgrims, the canyon's floor is also home to a dangerous snake-like creature known as a Goldpebble.⁠
2128080003:
Azari Palace

The Azari Palace is an ossified remnant of the period when worship of Aroden was a prominent feature of life in Absalom, before his death and the dawn of the Age of Lost Omens. Aroden's church was once an integral part of civic life in the City at the Centre of the World, but, with his passing in 4606 AR, his followers fell to infighting and despair. Many worshippers converted to other faiths, but 5,000 years of history, relics, and influence do not disperse quite as easily. The Azari Palace is the physical embodiment of this. Once called Saint Solian Temple, it once served as the second-largest temple of Aroden in the Ascendant Court; the largest ex-cathedral in the district now serves as the Chelaxian embassy.⁠ Nevertheless, it is still one of the district's most beautiful buildings.⁠

Azari Palace is named after its owners, House Azari, one of Absalom's numerous noble houses that traces its roots back to one of Aroden's earliest disciples and was intrinsically linked to Aroden's church. Dozens of House Azari's scions were elected to lead the church of Aroden, and three members of the house, including St. Solian, ascended to become saints of Aroden's religion. House Azari's support of the crumbling church of Aroden cost them everything, bankrupting the family and forcing them to sell their palatial estate in the Petal District. Led by house patriarch Lord Toiden, they moved into St. Solian Temple instead.⁠

As more and more churches and temples of Aroden have closed, the Azari Palace has become a vast repository for relics and artifacts of the now-dead religion. With no new worshippers coming to the faith and House Azari fallen in all but name, the Azari Palace has a feeling of forlorn abandonment, with near-endless chambers of dusty relics and forlorn treasures left forgotten in a temple to a god that Golarion has moved on from.⁠
